explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but God says the opposite. He says, “…I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people…” (Exodus 33:3). He does promise an angel to go before them, but He says He Himself won't be making the trip. That's a heavy thing to hear.

That's right. God says, “…I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people…” (Exodus 33:3). He does say He will send an angel before them, but He Himself won't be going along. I think that line landed hard on everyone who heard it.

Yes, friend. God says He won't go with them “otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). A few verses later He says it again: “If I should go with you for a single moment, I would destroy you.” (Exodus 33:5). He says it twice, so it's clearly worth catching.

I see why you'd pick it, but test isn't the word in this verse. God says “otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). That's a much heavier word than test. He says it again two verses later: “If I should go with you for a single moment, I would destroy you.” (Exodus 33:5).

Scatter is what my sprinkles do every time I sneeze. But God doesn't use that word here. He says if He went with them, “…I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). It's a heavy word, and it's the one the verse uses.

Yes, friend. The verse says “…no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). The people had just heard the bad news, and they went into mourning. Then verse 6 says the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.

Sandals never come up, friend. The verse says the people “…went into mourning, and no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). The only thing it names is jewelry. I'll keep my sandals out of this one anyway, since I'm a stamper standing on a gold base.

Armor is a bold guess, friend, but it isn't in this verse. The people heard bad news, and the text says they “…went into mourning, and no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). The word that fits the blank is jewelry.

explanations.answer: Decide what to do with them
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, “Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.” (Exodus 33:5). He doesn't say what He'll decide yet. We just have to wait and see, so keep reading.

The text never says that. The LORD says, “Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.” (Exodus 33:5). He leaves the decision open, so the verse doesn't give any answer yet. Egypt isn't mentioned at all.

explanations.answer: Choose a new leader for them
explanations.explanation: Nope, and Moses is still the one God is talking to in this scene. What the LORD says is, “Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.” (Exodus 33:5). Nothing about swapping leaders. The verse keeps the decision open.

Yes! The text says, “…anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.” (Exodus 33:7). Anyone. The tent isn't kept for a short list of important names. If you wanted to ask the LORD something, you walked out there.

That list is way too short, baker. The verse says “…anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.” (Exodus 33:7). The word is anyone, and it doesn't name two people. I'd say the door was open to whoever came asking.

The verse doesn't put a limit like that on it. It says “…anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.” (Exodus 33:7). Anyone is a big word. It doesn't mention any group that gets in first.

Yes, baker! “As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). The cloud settles at the door, and then the LORD speaks. Verse 7 says anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to this tent outside the camp. Moses walks in, and he isn't left standing there wondering.

The verse doesn't say anything like that. What happens is, “…the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). Moses goes in, and the LORD speaks with him. No altar is mentioned.

Nice try, friend, but this verse doesn't mention a pen or any writing. It says, “…the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). Moses goes in, the cloud comes down, and the LORD speaks with him. The verse gives us a conversation, nothing more.

Yes, friend. “When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.” (Exodus 33:10). They didn't have to walk to the tent. Verse 8 says they would stand at their own tent entrances and watch Moses until he went in, so they were already right there. Front row seats, and nobody had to fight for parking.

It's actually true. Verse 10 says, “…they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.” (Exodus 33:10). When they saw the cloud, they stood up and worshiped right at their own tent entrances.

explanations.answer: Face to face like a friend
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That line is the heart of the scene. It's like two friends talking across the counter, with nobody in between. Right after it, Moses speaks to the LORD (Exodus 33:12), and the LORD answers him (Exodus 33:14).
The verse says something else. “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That's a lot closer than a dream. Nobody had to wait for bedtime.
This verse leaves Aaron out of it. It says, “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). Face to face means no go-between.

That's him! “…his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11). Moses heads back to camp, but Joshua stays put in the tent. The text doesn't say why he stayed, and I'd love to know. I bet I would have stayed too, wouldn't you?

Caleb is one of the twelve spies who scouted Canaan (Numbers 13:6), but he's not the name here. The verse says “…his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11). Joshua is Moses's young assistant.

Eleazar was one of Aaron's sons (Exodus 6:23), but the verse doesn't name him. It says, “…his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11). Joshua is the name that goes in the blank.

Yes, friend. Moses says, “Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in My sight.’” (Exodus 33:12). Moses is reminding the LORD of what He already told him. Being known by name is a good thing to bring up.
It's actually true. Moses says, “Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in My sight.’” (Exodus 33:12). He brings it up as part of his request.

That's right. Moses says, “…please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight.” (Exodus 33:13). Moses is asking to know the LORD better, and that's a good thing to ask for. Then he adds, “Remember that this nation is Your people.” (Exodus 33:13). He asks for himself, and then he speaks up for the people.
It's actually true. Moses says, “…please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight.” (Exodus 33:13). He asks to know God's ways and to know God Himself.

explanations.answer: His Presence will go and give rest
explanations.explanation: Yes! The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Back in verse 3 He had said He would not go with them. Here He speaks of His own Presence going, and of rest. After all that bad news, rest is a nice word to hear.

explanations.answer: His prophets will go and guide them
explanations.explanation: That's not what He says, baker. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). He says His own Presence will go. There's no mention of prophets.

explanations.answer: Moses will go and lead them alone
explanations.explanation: Careful, baker, Moses isn't being sent off solo. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Notice who's doing the going: it's His own Presence. I think Moses was worried about who would go with him, since he says, “…You have not let me know whom You will send with me.” (Exodus 33:12). Walking a long road all by yourself sounds rough, and I bet he'd say so too.

explanations.answer: They have found favor in His sight
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Moses asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). Moses isn't asking for a trophy or a parade. He wants the proof of God's favor to be God Himself walking with them. If you've ever wanted the real thing and not just a nice sticker on the box, you get Moses here.

explanations.answer: They are the strongest nation on earth
explanations.explanation: Moses never talks about strength here. He asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). It's about favor in God's sight and not about being the strongest.

explanations.answer: Moses is the greatest leader of all
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say that. He asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). He's talking about favor in God's sight, for his people and himself. He's not bragging.

Yes, friend. Moses asks, “How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?” (Exodus 33:16). In his words, God going with them is what sets them apart from every other people. Think of a batch where one cookie is the only one stamped by the master. Everybody can tell which one it is.

It's actually true. Moses asks, “How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?” (Exodus 33:16). He says God going with them is what sets them apart from every other people.

Yes, baker. Moses says, “Please show me Your glory.” (Exodus 33:18). The LORD had just said yes to his last request in verse 17, and Moses asks for more. I'd have been nervous asking again, but Moses just asks it plainly.
A throne would be quite a sight, but it's not what Moses asks for. He says, “Please show me Your glory.” (Exodus 33:18). Glory is the word that goes in the blank.
Moses isn't asking for an army, baker. He says, “Please show me Your glory.” (Exodus 33:18). He wants to see the LORD's glory, and he doesn't ask for anything to fight with.

That's it, friend. Moses asked to see the LORD's glory, and the LORD answers by saying what He will do. First, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you…” (Exodus 33:19). Then He says He will proclaim His name, the LORD, with Moses standing right there to hear it.

A new set of laws would make a big announcement, but that's not what this verse says. The LORD says, “…I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence.” (Exodus 33:19). What gets proclaimed is His name, said right there with Moses. No rulebook this time, just the name.
No travel dates in this verse. The LORD says, “…I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence.” (Exodus 33:19). What He proclaims is His name, and nothing about when they leave.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). Moses can't see His face, and that's what makes the rock in the next verses matter.

That's right. The LORD says, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). He also says later, “…My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). So Moses is told he can't see His face.

explanations.answer: No one can see Him and live
explanations.explanation: That's right. The LORD says, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). That's the reason He gives, and it's a serious one. He doesn't say no and leave it there, though. In the next verses He tells Moses where to stand on a rock and what He will do (Exodus 33:21, 22, 23).
The LORD never says that. His reason is, “…no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). It's about no one being able to see Him and live, and it has nothing to do with Moses's job title.
The cloud isn't the reason in this verse. The LORD says, “…no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). That's the reason He gives for the face being off limits.

explanations.answer: Put him in the rock and cover him with His hand
explanations.explanation: Yes! The LORD says, “…I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.” (Exodus 33:22). A cleft is a crack in the rock. I think that sounds like a safe spot, with the LORD's own hand over you.

explanations.answer: Send him back inside the Tent of Meeting
explanations.explanation: The LORD doesn't say that here. He says, “…I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.” (Exodus 33:22). Moses stays at the rock, and the Tent of Meeting isn't mentioned.

explanations.answer: Tell him to close his eyes and kneel down
explanations.explanation: The LORD gives no instructions like that. He says, “…I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.” (Exodus 33:22). The LORD is the one doing the covering. Moses isn't asked to do anything but stand there.

Yes, baker! The LORD says, “Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). Before that, He says He will put Moses in a cleft of the rock and cover him with His hand until He has passed by (Exodus 33:22). So Moses gets covered first, then he sees. I think if I were standing in that rock, I'd be holding very, very still.

Feet is a fun guess, and I love a fun guess, but the LORD doesn't use that word. He says, “…you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). Verse 22 has His hand covering Moses until He has passed by, and then the hand comes away. The word that goes in the blank is back.
Close, but side isn't the word. The LORD says, “…you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). The word is back, and the face stays unseen.
